findings.message:
We need at least one Release/Acquire operation so that `Cursor` can see a valid page table node created by `CursorMut`. Otherwise, due to the lack of Release/Acquire synchronization, `Cursor` may see a garbage page that contains nothing valid.

 - Neither `PodOnce` nor `read_volatile`/`write_volatile` can provide this Release/Acquire semantics, so I think it is literally wrong to do this.

[Also, `read_volatile`/`write_volatile` cannot solve a data race problem at all.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/std/ptr/fn.read_volatile.html#safety) I think the official Miri feels the same way. While we can suppress such warnings on untyped memory, I don't think page tables are untyped. So if volatile operations cause data races on page tables, I think KernMiri should report them as soundness problems.
findings.tp_fp_justification: lrh2000 (reply in thread rooted at tatetian's question 1947498949): PodOnce's volatile read/write does not eliminate the data race nor provide Release/Acquire ordering, so a concurrent reader can observe a garbage page-table node pointer. Author accepts. The separate check-then-link concern (1947436045) was resolved by the author (lock already held) and is not recorded.
